evidence.why_not_priced: The preview literature is still quoting the 15% back-half rate as fact and framing it as the central risk — a 2026-09-08 preview is titled 'American Eagle Needs 81% Of Its Year In The Back Half — While The Tariff Rate Steps Up' and builds its whole bear case on the 10%-to-15% step-up, one day before the print. If the market had reconciled AEO's May assumption against the July 24 statutory replacement, that preview could not have been written that way, the 25-delta skew would not be +6.6 puts-bid, and the stock would not be trading 38.9% below its 52-week high on a plan whose largest stated cost headwind is roughly 3-4 points of receipt value lighter than budgeted. AEO set the number before the regime existed and reaffirmed it on 2026-07-01, three weeks before the change.
evidence.independence: Independent confirmation of the same regime change from a different publisher: https://www.tariffstool.com/tariffs-from-vietnam (last updated 2026-08-24) states Vietnam is 12.5% under the Section 301 forced-labor tariff effective 2026-07-24, replacing Section 122. The company-side anchor is a separate document, https://www.aeo-inc.com/2026/05/28/american-eagle-outfitters-reports-first-quarter-results-5/ (2026-05-28), whose guidance footnote states the 10%/15% assumption.

evidence.text: AEO will report GAAP EPS several times the $0.21 consensus purely mechanically — it told CNBC on 2026-06-03 it had already received $108m of IEEPA refunds, its 10-Q says the amount plus any further refunds will be recorded as a reduction of cost of sales for the 13 weeks ending 2026-08-01, and guidance explicitly excludes it — but the 2Q26 retail season's own base rate is that the market strips these out: Kohl's fell about 6% on a $150m refund and a raised full-year outlook, Target's stock fell on a beat containing $1.65/share of refund, and the only large positive reaction (ANF +36%) came with a 23% underlying beat ex-refund.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a correction to a mispricing of the *reaction function*, not of the fact. AEO's own tape shows the read-across is unresolved: the stock rose 5.14% on 2026-08-26 (ANF's refund-driven print) and gave back 5.12% on 2026-08-27, a clean round trip to zero, and the 20-day run-up is -0.78%. That pattern is what an unsettled question looks like, not a priced one. If the market had settled it in the bullish direction the run-up would be positive and the skew would be call-bid; if it had settled it bearishly there would be no 5% up-day. The consequence is that the near-certain 3x headline beat is not the catalyst a naive reading of the six-estimate consensus implies, and the resulting full-year operating-income raise from ~$390-410m to ~$500m+ will be discounted as a non-recurring item that has to be lapped in 2027.
evidence.independence: Coresight's 2026-09-08 survey of 2Q26 refund bookings and the guidance split across Walmart, Target, TJX, Ross, Dollar Tree, Dollar General, Lululemon, Deckers, Crocs and Levi's points the same way from a different publisher: https://coresight.com/research/tariff-refunds-in-2q26-billions-booked-by-retailers-and-brands-guidance-split/ . The AEO-specific refund fact is from a separate source again, https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/06/03/american-eagle-outfitters-says-it-has-received-108-million-in-tariff-refunds-so-far.html (2026-06-03).

evidence.text: Ravi Thanawala became AEO's CFO effective 2026-08-03 — two days after the quarter being reported closed on 2026-08-01 — succeeding Mike Mathias after 25 years, and tonight is his first earnings call; he inherits, without having set it, a full-year plan whose arithmetic requires $324.5m of the $390-410m operating-income guide (81.1%) to land in the back half, a 4.3x ramp off $75.5m of first-half operating income.
evidence.why_not_priced: The CFO change was covered as a personnel story in early July and has not been connected to the shape of the guide it lands on top of. Every preview I found — including the 2026-09-08 one that does the 81.1% arithmetic — treats the back-half loading as a pure operating question and does not mention that the person who now owns that number started 37 days ago and did not build it. If the market had connected them, the coverage would frame tonight as a rebasing event rather than a beat-or-miss on $0.21, and a stock 38.9% off its high with a plan needing a 4.3x second-half ramp would carry more than a 6.6-point 25-delta skew on 188% ATM implied vol, which is proportionally flat for an event of this kind. Note the offset that is genuinely priced: the company reaffirmed both Q2 and full-year guidance in this same release on 2026-07-01, which caps how bad the Q2 underlying can plausibly be.
evidence.independence: The 81.1% back-half arithmetic is from a different source and a different date: https://tradesandgains.substack.com/p/american-eagle-needs-81-of-its-year (2026-09-08), which computes $75.5m first-half versus $324.5m implied second-half operating income. evidence.text: Culp issued its Q1 FY27 guidance on 2026-07-01 for a quarter that ended 2026-08-02 - i.e. with roughly 9 of 13 weeks already elapsed and the $7.0m tariff refund cash already in hand - so 'breakeven to positive adjusted EBITDA without the benefit of IEEPA tariff refunds' and 'net debt of approximately $5.0 million by first quarter-end' are near-observed facts, not forecasts.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline's expected move is a 6.02% median drawn from seven prints of which six went down - all of them delivered mid-restructuring with no forward guidance and genuinely uncertain outcomes. If the market had processed that the outcome distribution is narrow, the run-up would not be a directionless -0.58% over 20 days and the 5-day drift would not be a 17,000-share-a-day random walk; a stock about to resolve a genuinely uncertain 6% event trades differently into it.
